title: SseFrame is non_exhaustive but not Clone; callers cannot store frames
description: SseFrame is #[non_exhaustive] and #[derive(Debug)] but not Clone. SseEvent is Clone. A caller who receives an SseFrame from subscribe_events and wants to store it for later processing (e.g. a buffer, a channel, a select! arm) cannot clone it. They must either destructure it immediately or use Arc<SseFrame>. This is an ergonomic trap: SseEvent is Clone so callers might expect SseFrame to be too. The missing Clone derive is a source of confusing compiler errors for downstream users. Since SseFrame is #[non_exhaustive], adding Clone later is not a breaking change, but omitting it now causes friction. Add Clone to SseFrame.
